symptom: `grant read * on entity Shop.Item to Shop.User where [Name = 'a' or Name = 'b'];` followed by the same grant with the XPath wrapped over two lines left two identical rules; diff reported a change, and on a real project upgraded from nightly-20261020 to nightly-20261117 every re-run duplicated two grants stored on one line by the older build.
file: mdl/types/xpath_same.go SameXPathConstraint; mdl/backend/modelsdk/domainmodel_security_write.go AddEntityAccessRule (match + keep stored spelling); mdl/executor/cmd_entities_access.go formatAccessRuleResult. Test: mdl/backend/modelsdk/access_rule_xpath_spacing_2355_test.go
cause: The upsert key (role set + constraint, #936) compared the constraint byte for byte, and FormatXPathConstraint keeps a constraint that already fits as written, so a script's line break reached both the comparison and the stored value.
insight: **A string that is part of an identity key must be compared in its canonical form, and a match must keep the stored spelling.** Comparing whitespace-insensitively outside literals (the same rule canon's CarryUnexpressed already applies to XPath) merges the grants; writing back the stored constraint on a match is what makes the re-run elide instead of rewriting the rule in the new spelling. Control: whitespace inside a string literal still distinguishes rules. Live on 11.12.6: the reporter's a.mdl then b.mdl gives one rule, diff 'exec would write nothing', exec 'Unchanged entity access'.
